title: Visitor Badge Expiry Tracking
exclusions: Exclude development and lab VMS tenants that reuse production `visitor_id` namespaces, and exclude visitor types tagged `simulation=true` used for access-control regression testing.
evidence: Alert result set CSV, Splunk job inspector showing `resultCount`, and a screenshot or API export from the Visitor management system proving the matched `visitor_id` was deactivated after remediation.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=physical` sourcetype='vms:visitor' where `entity` satisfies `days_to_exp` < 0 for UC-15.3.17 ('Visitor Badge Expiry Tracking'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `physical` / `vms:visitor` events where `entity` stays below `days_to_exp` < 0, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-15.3.17.

dataSources: Land normalised visitor or badge payloads from your **Visitor management system API** HTTPS source into `index=physical` as `sourcetype="vms:visitor"` with extracted fields `visitor_id`, `badge_expiry`, `status`, and `host_employee` (plus any vendor-supplied sync metadata such as batch or ETag). Use the Splunk **REST API Modular Input** ([Splunkbase app ID 1747](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1747)) or an approved scripted poller that calls the vendor `/visitors`, `/badges`, or equivalent read-only endpoints on a one- to five-minute interval, storing credentials in `password` stanzas or a secrets manager—never in dashboard tokens. Forwarders should tag `meta` sourcetype overrides in `props.conf` so search-time `strptime(badge_expiry,"%Y-%m-%d")` aligns with the API’s date format.
spl:
index=physical sourcetype="vms:visitor"
| eval days_to_exp=round((strptime(badge_expiry,"%Y-%m-%d")-now())/86400,0)
| where status="active" AND (days_to_exp < 0 OR days_to_exp < 1)
| table visitor_id, host_employee, badge_expiry, days_to_exp
description: Detects visitor-credential rows on the `vms:visitor` feed where `status` remains active while `badge_expiry` is already in the past or due within twenty-four hours, signalling that deprovisioning never reached the logical visitor record Splunk indexes for the controlled facility.
value: Detects visitor-credential rows on the `vms:visitor` feed where `status` remains active while `badge_expiry.... Timely UC-15.3.17 alerting on 'Visitor Badge Expiry Tracking' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Onboard visitor or badge REST/JSON extracts from the Visitor management system API into `index=physical` with `sourcetype="vms:visitor"`; schedule the REST modular input or HEC/scripted forwarder at least hourly for compliance baselines and every five minutes where mantrap risk is high; normalise `badge_expiry`, `visitor_id`, `status`, and escort metadata; reconcile daily with PACS cardholder tables when the API mirrors are delayed; save the expiry search as a scheduled alert with thirty-minute suppression on `visitor_id` and route to physical security operations.
visualization: Primary Table panel listing `visitor_id`, `host_employee`, `badge_expiry`, and `days_to_exp` sorted by worst drift; paired Single Value for `count` of offending badges; Timeline of expiring-not-yet-disabled events by hour; optional Map or location field if `data_hall` exists in extended props.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  by Authentication.user, Authentication.action, Authentication.src span=1h
| sort - count
dataModelAcceleration: Accelerate the Authentication data model only after `vms:visitor` events are fully CIM-mapped via `eventtypes`/`tags`; otherwise keep acceleration off and rely on raw `index=physical` fast search plus summary indexing if volume exceeds tens of millions of daily visitor rows.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `physical`** — Planned work for 'Visitor Badge Expiry Tracking' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-15.3.17. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `vms:visitor`** — Scheduled automation elevates `days_to_exp` without crossing `days_to_exp` < 0. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `vms:visitor`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
equipmentModels: Visitor management system API visitor feed (vms:visitor)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud search head with the **REST API Modular Input** ([Splunkbase app 1747](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1747)) or an internal HEC relay already approved by your InfoSec team.
• Network path and service account able to reach the Visitor management system API `https://<vms-host>/...` endpoints with read-only OAuth2 client credentials or API keys stored under `storage/passwords`.
• RBAC: grant `indexes_search` on `physical` and `dispatch_rest_to_indexers` only to the `physical_security_analyst` role (map to `sc_admin` patterns on Splunk Cloud).
• Confirmed field contract: `visitor_id`, `badge_expiry`, `status`, `host_employee` on `sourcetype="vms:visitor"` matching the sample Event rendered in Search.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create a REST input stanza (or Modular Input UI entry) targeting the visitor export, set polling interval `60s`–`300s`, and write JSON events to `index=physical` with `sourcetype="vms:visitor"`. In `props.conf`, assign `KV_MODE=json` if the payload is JSON, and set `TIME_PREFIX`/`TIME_FORMAT` if the vendor supplies event time separate from `_time`. Document the canonical `badge_expiry` string format (`%Y-%m-%d` vs ISO-8601) beside the input.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Paste the saved SPL from this use case into Search, verify row counts against the vendor UI for the same `/visitors?status=active` filter, then save as an alert with `dispatch.earliest_time=-24h` and `dispatch.latest_time=now` to catch badges that expired within the last day while still marked active.

Understanding this SPL (no query edits in this workflow)
• `index=physical` and `sourcetype="vms:visitor"` anchor the search to the visitor feed described under Data sources.
• `eval days_to_exp` turns `badge_expiry` into a drift metric comparable to `now()`.
• `where status="active" AND (days_to_exp < 0 OR days_to_exp < 1)` isolates credentials that should already be inactive or are within the policy buffer window.
• `table visitor_id, host_employee, badge_expiry, days_to_exp` is the analyst payload for PACS reconciliation.

Step 3 — Validate
Spot-check five `visitor_id` values against the Visitor management system admin console and against a mantrap reader denial log (`expired credential`) for the same fifteen-minute window; mismatch indicates sync lag rather than a true breach.

Step 4 — Operationalise
Publish the alert summary to a Physical Access dashboard with drilldown on `visitor_id`, attach a runbook link in the notable description, and yearly review cron schedules versus audit sampling periods.
